residual_risk: The mermaid block was reviewed against mermaid's documented grammar but never rendered: browser automation and `npm install mermaid` were both denied in this session. The diagram is embedded in the PR body, README.md and protocol.md, so GitHub renders it on the PR page — that is the first check a reviewer should make.

Mermaid's handling of #60;/#62; is the uncertain part: if it decodes to a raw `<` before the label becomes HTML, angle brackets in a title still vanish. No worse than leaving them raw (DOMPurify strips the tag either way), but protocol.md states the intent as if it always works.
hkb graph is not exposed as an MCP tool (src/mcp.js untouched) — out of scope here, cheap to add later.
Titles clip at 56 characters, so two long titles differing only after char 56 render alike; the issue number in the label disambiguates them.
docs/wiki/ freshness: three pages report stale on blob SHAs and were left alone, with the reasoning in the summary.
verification: npm test — 581 tests, 0 fail (9 new in test/track.test.js)
npm run smoke — the packed tarball installs, runs, and hkb init copies the bumped skill

results.summary:
hkb graph <n> [--mermaid] [--json] emits the track rooted at <n> as one fenced mermaid block; PR #111 (draft, Closes #109).

Three pure functions in src/track.js: trackGraph(track) -> {root, nodes, edges, cycle} built from resolveTrack/trackWaves (no second walk of the dependency graph), trackMermaid(graph) -> the fenced `flowchart TD`, mermaidLabel(text) -> the escaping. src/cli.js gets a `graph` case (one fetchBoard, then resolveTrack; a usage error naming `hkb list` when the number is not on the board), 'mermaid' added to BOOL_FLAGS so `hkb graph --mermaid 12` keeps 12 as the positional, and a help entry.

The bare command IS the diagram — `--mermaid` is the explicit spelling of the default — so `hkb comment 12 "$(hkb graph 12)"` works as the task's integration note requires (hkb comment still does not read stdin; it was not extended). `--json` returns {root, nodes, edges, cycle, mermaid} where `mermaid` is byte-identical to what the command prints, fence included; a test asserts that.

Both prototype defects are fixed. `#` -> `#35;`, escaped FIRST because it is the escape character (escaping it last would eat the codes the others write), then `"` -> `#quot;` and `<`/`>` -> `#60;`/`#62;` — labels are HTML, so `<n>` in a title is otherwise swallowed as a tag. Titles clip at 56 chars. classDefs set stroke/width/dash and NOTHING else — a test asserts `fill:` and `color:` never appear in the output — so GitHub's dark mermaid theme and its light one both keep readable labels.

Arrows run blocker -> what it unblocks, so the frontier is on top and the root is last, drawn as a stadium. A blocker closed as completed is not drawn (the picture shrinks with the track, exactly as resolveTrack does); an unfinished blocker that is not on this board IS drawn, dashed, as "not on this board", so a hole in the graph is visible rather than silently missing.

Docs: /kanban:decompose step (e) appends `hkb graph <root>` to the notes it comments on the goal, and "check your work" now leads with it (skills/kanban/SKILL.md, version 0.5.0 -> 0.5.1, with the assertion in test/track.test.js moved to match); skills/kanban/references/protocol.md gains a "The graph as a diagram" subsection under Decomposition-worked, showing the real output; README.md gains "The dependency graph as a diagram: hkb graph".
